messages:
Maya (Support): heads-up: acme-app (CS-98321) reporting p99 embed latency spike in eu1 since last night maintenance, p95 fine but p99 from ~220ms -> ~1.8s. customer unhappy, escalated.
Ajay (Eng-Infra): can you paste a repro / example request + timestamps? which nodes are serving them? link to traces? :eyes:
Maya (Support): here's a sample curl we used and a trace span: curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings -d '{\"input\":\"hello\"}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer <redacted>'
Maya (Support): trace link: https://internal.traces/reports/CS-98321 (they included p99 spike around 2025-10-12T03:12Z). customer says started after maintenance window (kernel + driver roll).
Lee (Eng-SRE): quick check: last kernel roll was pushed 2025-10-12 02:40Z and CUDA driver updated on the same window. I see several eu1 hosts showed NVMe queue-depth growth and hostfs latencies in metrics.
Lee (Eng-SRE): running on one impacted node: run `iostat -x 1 3` and `dmesg | tail -n 50` — any lots of `blk_update_request` or timeouts?
Ajay (Eng-Infra): looked at node eu1-nd-17 (serving that customer). iostat shows util ~98% for nvme0n1 and avgqu-sz high. blkio cgroup shows some pods with bursty writes (not the LLM pods). suspect storage interference.
Maya (Support): customer says they only call embeddings sync small payloads — low write. we saw p99 jump even on read-heavy batches.
Noah (Product): customer impact: multiple requests timed out and retried, double-billing complaints. we need immediate mitigations and a short update to CS.
Ajay (Eng-Infra): immediate mitigations we can do now:
- move CS-98321 traffic to eu1-dedicated-pool (route-by-customer) to isolate (fast)
- pin their model variant to quantized small variant to reduce GPU memory pressure
- throttle blkio for noisy tenants on eu1-nd-*
- fallback policy: route to eu2 if latency > 1s for > 3s
Lee (Eng-SRE): I'll grab the node and enable temporary blkio throttling for the noisy pod, and roll back kernel on 3 busiest hosts to previous build (rollback plan in playbook).
Ajay (Eng-Infra): also found a regression in nvme driver with our new I/O scheduler + CUDA pinned memory behavior: KV cache warmups are causing synchronous eviction writes. patch candidate to limit warmup concurrency available.
Maya (Support): CS update drafted: "we've isolated increased host-level IO contention after our maintenance window and are applying mitigations (routing and host-level throttles). We'll follow up with root-cause and ETA for full remediation." sending now.
Deploy-Bot: rollback-job/1759 started for eu1 nodes {eu1-nd-05, eu1-nd-09, eu1-nd-17}
Infra-Bot: route update: CS-98321 traffic moved to eu1-dedicated-pool at 2025-10-12T04:05Z
Lee (Eng-SRE): quick datapoint: after moving traffic + throttling noisy pod p99 for that customer dropped from ~1.8s -> ~260ms within ~60s. still monitoring for regressions.
Ajay (Eng-Infra): plan for full fix: revert problematic nvme scheduler config + land nvme driver backport once validated, and add cgroup blkio safeguards to prevent eviction storms. schedule across eu1 gradually.
Noah (Product): action items:
- Ajay/Lee: complete rollback + driver backport (P0) and confirm across eu1 (ETA 4h)
- Maya: keep CS-98321 updated every 30m until stable
- Infra: add automated detection alert for hostfs avgqu-sz > X and auto-mitigate route/fallback
Maya (Support): noted, updating customer now. ticket CS-98321 updated with mitigation notes and reduced SLO impact window. :white_check_mark:
Lee (Eng-SRE): logging action: capture `iostat -x`, `pidstat -d`, `dmesg` snapshots and attach to postmortem. I'll create incident page and link here.
Maya (Support): thanks all — will close the customer loop once we confirm 1hr stable. :pray:
Deploy-Bot: rollback-job/1759 completed on eu1 nodes (success)
Lee (Eng-SRE): last check: p99 steady ~240-300ms for CS-98321, marking as mitigated. will keep open until driver backport lands.
Maya (Support): closing update: customer confirmed improved latency, happy with temporary fixes. leaving open for RCA + postmortem.
